translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor specially ordered Ding to preside over the provincial examination and, while there, take charge of the case. His investigation revealed that the Xu family had once been wealthy; officials had used the lawsuit to ruin their estate, many had taken bribes, and collusion and concealment had made the facts of the case confused and fantastical.

sentences.zh: 悉發其覆，置之法，浙人稱頌焉。

translations.literal: He exposed every cover-up, punished the guilty according to law, and the people of Zhejiang praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed every hidden scheme, punished the guilty according to law, and the people of Zhejiang praised him.

sentences.zh: 六年，授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，回疆平，以贊畫功，加太子太保，繪像紫光閣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, after the pacification of the Western Regions, for his contributions to planning he was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and had his portrait painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the pacification of the Western Regions, he was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent for his contributions to planning, and his portrait was painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 蘆鹽積疲，商累日重，命鼎偕侍郎敬徵察辦。

translations.literal: Changlu salt had long been declining, and the merchants' burdens grew daily. Ding was ordered together with Vice Minister Jing Zheng to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu salt had long been in decline, and the merchants' burdens grew heavier by the day. Ding was ordered together with Vice Minister Jing Zheng to investigate and handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 議以；

translations.literal: After deliberation they proposed:
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation they proposed:

sentences.zh: 「鹽務首重年清年款，先將節年帶徵釐剔，現年正款不難按數清完。

translations.literal: " Salt administration should above all emphasize clearing each year's accounts on schedule. First eliminate the carried-over supplementary levies from past years, and the current year's principal receipts will not be difficult to settle in full.
translations.idiomatic: " Salt administration should above all emphasize clearing each year's accounts on schedule. First eliminate the carried-over supplementary levies from past years, and the current year's principal receipts will not be difficult to settle in full.

sentences.zh: 道光二年以前未完銀九百餘萬為舊欠，三年以後未完銀為新欠，緩舊徵新。

translations.literal: Uncollected silver before the second year of Daoguang, totaling more than nine million, should be classified as old arrears; uncollected silver after the third year should be classified as new arrears, with collection of old arrears deferred while new arrears are pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Uncollected silver before the second year of the Daoguang reign, totaling more than nine million, should be classified as old arrears; uncollected silver after the third year should be classified as new arrears, with collection of old arrears deferred while new arrears are pursued.

sentences.zh: 請以堰工加價二文，半解部充公，半抵完商欠。

translations.literal: Request that an additional two cash be added to dike-work surcharges, half remitted to the ministry for public funds and half applied to clearing merchants' arrears.
translations.idiomatic: They requested that an additional two cash be added to dike-work surcharges, half remitted to the ministry for public funds and half applied to clearing merchants' arrears.

sentences.zh: 新欠抵完，續抵舊欠。

translations.literal: Once new arrears are cleared, continue paying down old arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Once new arrears are cleared, continue paying down old arrears.

sentences.zh: 蘆商生息帑本內，直隸水利、趙北口兩項非經費歲需，請停利三年。

translations.literal: Within the interest-bearing treasury principal of the Changlu salt merchants, the items for Zhili waterworks and Zhaobeikou are not annual operating expenses; request a three-year suspension of interest.
translations.idiomatic: Within the interest-bearing treasury principal of the Changlu salt merchants, the items for Zhili waterworks and Zhaobeikou are not annual operating expenses; they requested a three-year suspension of interest.

sentences.zh: 限滿加一倍利，本息同徵。

translations.literal: When the term expires, add interest at double the rate and collect principal and interest together.
translations.idiomatic: When the term expires, interest at double the rate would be added and principal and interest collected together.

sentences.zh: 舊有拔繳水利帑本一百十七萬兩，請停徵三年。

translations.literal: Of the old waterworks treasury principal of 1.17 million taels that had been assigned for collection, request a three-year suspension of collection.
translations.idiomatic: Of the old waterworks treasury principal of 1.17 million taels that had been assigned for collection, they requested a three-year suspension of collection.

sentences.zh: 自道光十一年起，歲徵十萬兩，五萬完舊本，五萬完新本，以卹商力。

translations.literal: Starting from the eleventh year of Daoguang, collect 100,000 taels per year—50,000 to clear old principal and 50,000 to clear new principal—to relieve the merchants' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from the eleventh year of the Daoguang reign, 100,000 taels would be collected each year—50,000 to clear old principal and 50,000 to clear new principal—to relieve the merchants' burden.

sentences.zh: 近年商力疲乏，不能預買生鹽，存坨新鹽多滷耗。

translations.literal: In recent years merchants' resources have been exhausted; they cannot pre-purchase raw salt in advance, and stockpiled new salt at the yards suffers much brine loss.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the merchants' resources had been exhausted; they could not pre-purchase raw salt in advance, and stockpiled new salt at the yards suffered much brine loss.

sentences.zh: 請每包加鹽十三斤，俾資貼補，從此款目既清，庶經久可行。」

translations.literal: Request adding thirteen jin of salt to each bundle to provide compensation; once these accounts are cleared in this way, the system may endure."
translations.idiomatic: They requested adding thirteen jin of salt to each bundle to provide compensation; once these accounts were cleared in this way, the system might endure."

sentences.zh: 又請免繳嘉慶十七年加價交官半文未完銀一百八十四萬餘兩。

translations.literal: They also requested exemption from payment of more than 1.84 million taels in uncollected silver from the half-cash surcharge added in the seventeenth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested exemption from payment of more than 1.84 million taels in uncollected silver from the half-cash surcharge added in the seventeenth year of the Jiaqing reign.

sentences.zh: 疏入，並允行。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, all measures were approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, all measures were approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，蘆商呈請調劑，復命鼎及侍郎寶興往按。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Changlu salt merchants petitioned for adjustments, and Ding together with Vice Minister Bao Xing were again ordered to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Changlu salt merchants petitioned for adjustments, and Ding together with Vice Minister Bao Xing were again ordered to investigate on site.

sentences.zh: 鼎以前次清查，傳集各商詳詢定議，皆稱可免虧累積壓，雖因銀價漸昂，尚不致遽形虧折，遂議駁。

translations.literal: Ding, based on the previous investigation, summoned all merchants for detailed inquiry and deliberation. All agreed they could avoid cumulative losses and stockpiling; although the price of silver was gradually rising, losses would not quickly become apparent. He therefore recommended rejection of the petition.
translations.idiomatic: Based on the previous investigation, Ding summoned all the merchants for detailed inquiry and deliberation. All agreed they could avoid cumulative losses and stockpiling; although the price of silver was gradually rising, losses would not quickly become apparent. He therefore recommended rejecting the petition.

sentences.zh: 時淮鹽尤敝，兩江總督陶澍疏陳積弊情形，命鼎偕寶興會同籌議。

translations.literal: At that time Huai salt was especially run-down. Governor-General Tao Shu of the Two Jiangs memorialized on the accumulated abuses, and Ding together with Bao Xing were ordered to join in deliberating reforms.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huai salt was especially run-down. Governor-General Tao Shu of the Two Jiangs memorialized on the accumulated abuses, and Ding together with Bao Xing were ordered to join in deliberating reforms.

sentences.zh: 中外論鹽事者，多主就場徵稅。

translations.literal: Those inside and outside the court discussing salt affairs mostly favored collecting tax at the production sites.
translations.idiomatic: Those inside and outside the court discussing salt affairs mostly favored collecting tax at the production sites.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「詳覈淮綱全局，若改課歸場灶，尚多窒兒。

translations.literal: They memorialized: "Upon thorough review of the overall Huai salt system, if tax collection were shifted back to the salt fields and furnaces, many difficulties would remain.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized: "Upon thorough review of the overall Huai salt system, if tax collection were shifted back to the salt fields and furnaces, many difficulties would remain.

sentences.zh: 惟有就舊章大加釐剔，使射利者無可藉端，欠課者無可藉口，似較有往轍可循。

translations.literal: Only by greatly refining and pruning the old regulations, so that those seeking profit have no pretext and those owing taxes have no excuse, would there seem to be a workable path to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Only by greatly refining and pruning the old regulations, so that those seeking profit had no pretext and those owing taxes had no excuse, would there seem to be a workable path to follow.

sentences.zh: 擬定章程十五條，曰：裁浮費，減窩價，刪繁文，慎出納，裁商總，覈滯銷，緩積欠，卹灶丁，給船價，究淹銷，疏運道，添岸店，散輪規，飭紀綱，收灶鹽。」

translations.literal: They drafted fifteen regulations, namely: cut superfluous expenses, reduce depot prices, delete redundant paperwork, be careful in receipts and disbursements, abolish merchant syndicate heads, verify stagnant sales, defer accumulated arrears, relieve salt-furnace laborers, pay boat freight, investigate smuggled salt, improve transport routes, add shore depots, break up rotation rules, enforce discipline, and collect salt from the furnaces."
translations.idiomatic: They drafted fifteen regulations, namely: cut superfluous expenses, reduce depot prices, delete redundant paperwork, be careful in receipts and disbursements, abolish merchant syndicate heads, verify stagnant sales, defer accumulated arrears, relieve salt-furnace laborers, pay boat freight, investigate smuggled salt, improve transport routes, add shore depots, break up rotation rules, enforce discipline, and collect salt from the furnaces."

sentences.zh: 又請裁撤兩淮鹽政，改歸總督辦理，以一事權。

translations.literal: They also requested abolishing the Lianghuai salt commissioner and transferring administration to the governor-general to unify authority.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested abolishing the Lianghuai salt commissioner and transferring administration to the governor-general to unify authority.

sentences.zh: 並詔允行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of this by decree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this by decree.

sentences.zh: 陶澍得銳意興革，淮綱自此漸振，鼎之力也。

translations.literal: Tao Shu was thus able to push reforms vigorously; the Huai salt system gradually revived from that point—the result of Ding's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shu was thus able to push reforms vigorously; the Huai salt system gradually revived from that point—the result of Ding's efforts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he acted as governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十二年，管理刑部事務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was placed in charge of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was placed in charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，協辦大學士，仍管刑部，直上書房。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he became associate grand secretary, still managing the Ministry of Justice, and entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became associate grand secretary, still managing the Ministry of Justice, and entered the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 二十年。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏，河決祥符，命偕侍郎慧成往治之，尋署河督。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year, the Yellow River breached at Xiangfu; he was ordered together with Vice Minister Huicheng to repair it, and soon acted as Director-General of River Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-first year, the Yellow River breached at Xiangfu; he was ordered together with Vice Minister Huicheng to repair it, and soon acted as Director-General of River Works.

sentences.zh: 議者以水勢方漲，不宜遽塞，請遷省城以避其衝，鼎持不可，疏言：「河灌歸德、陳州及安徽亳、潁，合淮東注洪澤湖，湖底日受淤。

translations.literal: Advisors, noting that the water was still rising, argued that the breach should not be blocked hastily and proposed moving the provincial capital to avoid the flood's force. Ding firmly objected and memorialized: "The river inundates Guide, Chen Prefecture, and Bozhou and Ying in Anhui; it joins the Huai and flows east into Hongze Lake, and the lake bed daily receives silt.
translations.idiomatic: Advisors, noting that the water was still rising, argued that the breach should not be blocked hastily and proposed moving the provincial capital to avoid the flood's force. Ding firmly objected and memorialized: "The river inundates Guide, Chen Prefecture, and Bozhou and Ying in Anhui; it joins the Huai and flows east into Hongze Lake, and the lake bed daily receives silt.

sentences.zh: 萬一宣洩不及，高堰危，淮、揚成巨浸，民其魚矣！

translations.literal: If discharge should prove insufficient, the High Dike would be endangered, Huaiyang would become a great floodplain, and the people would be fish in a net!
translations.idiomatic: If discharge should prove insufficient, the High Dike would be endangered, Huaiyang would become a great floodplain, and the people would be fish in a net!

sentences.zh: 無論舍舊址、築新堤數千里，工費不貲，且自古無任黃水橫流之理。

translations.literal: Not to mention that abandoning the old site and building new dikes for thousands of li would cost beyond reckoning—and since ancient times there has never been reason to allow the muddy Yellow River to flow unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Not to mention that abandoning the old site and building new dikes for thousands of li would cost beyond reckoning—and since ancient times there has never been reason to allow the muddy Yellow River to flow unchecked.

sentences.zh: 請飭戶部速具帑，期以冬春之交集事。

translations.literal: Request that the Ministry of Revenue quickly provide treasury funds, with work to be concentrated between winter and spring.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the Ministry of Revenue quickly provide treasury funds, with work to be concentrated between winter and spring.

sentences.zh: 不效，原執其咎。」

translations.literal: If this fails, I originally accept responsibility for the blame."
translations.idiomatic: If this fails, I accept responsibility for the blame."

sentences.zh: 具陳民情安土重遷、省垣可守狀。

translations.literal: He also set forth in detail the people's attachment to their native soil and reluctance to move, and the defensibility of the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth in detail the people's attachment to their native soil and reluctance to move, and the defensibility of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 初至汴城，四面皆水，旦夕且圮，躬率吏卒巡護，獲無恙。

translations.literal: When he first arrived at Bian Prefecture city, water surrounded it on all sides and collapse seemed imminent at any moment; he personally led officials and soldiers on patrol and guard, and the city remained unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived at Bian Prefecture city, water surrounded it on all sides and collapse seemed imminent at any moment; he personally led officials and soldiers on patrol and guard, and the city remained unscathed.

sentences.zh: 洎工興，親駐工次，倦則寢肩輿中。

translations.literal: When work began, he personally stationed himself at the worksite; when weary, he slept in his sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: When work began, he personally stationed himself at the worksite; when weary, he slept in his sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 次年二月，工竣，用帑六百萬有奇。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the work was completed, using more than six million in treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year the work was completed, using more than six million in treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 前此馬營工用一千二百餘萬，儀封工用四百七十五萬，原議以儀工為率。

translations.literal: Previously the Maying project had used more than 12 million, and the Yifeng project 4.75 million; the original plan had taken the Yifeng project as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Maying project had used more than 12 million, and the Yifeng project 4.75 million; the original plan had taken the Yifeng project as the standard.

sentences.zh: 及蕆事，加增百餘萬，然事艱於前，微鼎用節工速，不能如是。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, costs increased by more than a million, yet the task was harder than before; without Ding's economy and rapid completion, it could not have been done as it was.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed, costs increased by more than a million, yet the task was harder than before; without Ding's economy and rapid completion, it could not have been done as it was.

sentences.zh: 敘功，晉太子太師。

translations.literal: In recognition of merit he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 積勞成疾，命緩程回京。

translations.literal: Exhaustion from prolonged labor brought on illness, and he was ordered to return to the capital at a relaxed pace.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion from prolonged labor brought on illness, and he was ordered to return to the capital at a relaxed pace.

sentences.zh: 自禁煙事起，英吉利兵犯沿海，鼎力主戰。

translations.literal: From the time the opium prohibition began, when English troops attacked the coast, Ding strongly advocated war.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the opium prohibition began, when English troops attacked the coast, Ding strongly advocated war.

sentences.zh: 至和議將成，林則徐以罪譴，鼎憤甚，還朝爭之力，宣宗慰勞之，命休沐養疴。

translations.literal: When peace negotiations were nearing completion and Lin Zexu was punished and banished, Ding was deeply indignant and returned to court to argue his case with all his strength. The Daoguang Emperor consoled him and ordered him to take leave and rest to recover from illness.
translations.idiomatic: When peace negotiations were nearing completion and Lin Zexu was punished and banished, Ding was deeply indignant and returned to court to argue his case with all his strength. The Daoguang Emperor consoled him and ordered him to take leave and rest to recover from illness.

sentences.zh: 越數日，自草遺疏，劾大學士穆彰阿誤國，閉戶自縊，冀以屍諫。

translations.literal: A few days later he drafted a final memorial himself, impeaching Grand Secretary Mu Zhanga for misleading the state, then shut his door and hanged himself, hoping to remonstrate with his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he drafted a final memorial himself, impeaching Grand Secretary Mu Zhanga for misleading the state, then shut his door and hanged himself, hoping to remonstrate with his corpse.

sentences.zh: 軍機章京陳孚恩，穆彰阿黨也。

translations.literal: Chen Fuen, a Grand Council secretary, was a member of Mu Zhanga's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fuen, a Grand Council secretary, was a member of Mu Zhanga's faction.

sentences.zh: 滅其疏，別具以聞。

translations.literal: He destroyed the memorial and reported separately with another document.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the memorial and reported separately with another document.

sentences.zh: 上疑其卒暴，命取原不得，於是優詔憫惜，贈太保，諡文恪，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the suddenness of his death and ordered the original memorial retrieved but could not obtain it. Thereupon an exceptional edict expressed compassion, posthumously granted him the title of Grand Guardian, gave him the posthumous name Wenge, and enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected the suddenness of his death and ordered the original memorial retrieved but could not obtain it. Thereupon an exceptional edict expressed compassion, posthumously granted him the title of Grand Guardian, gave him the posthumous name Wenge, and enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 後陝西巡撫請祀鄉賢，特詔允之。

translations.literal: Later the Shaanxi governor requested enshrinement in the local worthies' temple, and a special edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shaanxi governor requested enshrinement in the local worthies' temple, and a special edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 鼎清操絕俗，生平不受請託，亦不請託於人。

translations.literal: Ding's integrity was extraordinary; throughout his life he neither accepted solicitations nor solicited others.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's integrity was extraordinary; throughout his life he neither accepted solicitations nor solicited others.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: On the day he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 子沆，道光二十年進士，翰林院編修。

translations.literal: His son Hang, a metropolitan graduate in the twentieth year of Daoguang, served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hang, a metropolitan graduate in the twentieth year of the Daoguang reign, served as compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿，字鶴舫，郭佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Mu Zhanga, style name Hefang, of the Guojia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zhanga, whose style was Hefang, of the Guojia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父廣泰，嘉慶中，官內閣學士，遷右翼總兵。

translations.literal: His father Guangtai, in the Jiaqing reign, held office as grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was later transferred to commander of the Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangtai, during the Jiaqing reign, held office as grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was later transferred to commander of the Right Wing.

sentences.zh: 坐自請兼兵部侍郎銜，奪職。

translations.literal: He was stripped of office for having voluntarily requested the concurrent designation of vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office for having voluntarily requested the concurrent designation of vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿，嘉慶十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Mu Zhanga, a metropolitan graduate in the tenth year of Jiaqing, was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zhanga, a metropolitan graduate in the tenth year of the Jiaqing reign, was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 大考，擢少詹事。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he was promoted to vice grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the grand examination he was promoted to vice grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十年，署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he acted as vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he acted as vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 因一日進立決本二十餘件，詔斥因循積壓，堂司各員並下嚴議，降光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Because in one day he forwarded more than twenty cases for immediate execution, an edict rebuked the delays and backlog; all chief and clerical officials were subjected to strict investigation, and he was demoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Because in one day he forwarded more than twenty cases for immediate execution, an edict rebuked the delays and backlog; all chief and clerical officials were subjected to strict investigation, and he was demoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、刑部、工部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice minister of War, Justice, Works, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice minister of War, Justice, Works, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 道光初，充內務府大臣，擢左都御史、理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he served as minister of the Imperial Household Department and was promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign he served as minister of the Imperial Household Department and was promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以漕船滯運，兩次命署漕運總督。

translations.literal: Because grain-transport ships were delayed, he was twice ordered to act as Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain-transport ships were delayed, he was twice ordered to act as Director-General of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 召授工部尚書，偕大學士蔣攸銛查勘南河。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed minister of Works, together with Grand Secretary Jiang Yinsuo he inspected the Southern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed minister of Works, and together with Grand Secretary Jiang Yinsuo he inspected the Southern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 洎試行海運，命赴天津監收漕糧，予優敘。

translations.literal: When sea transport was trial-tested, he was ordered to go to Tianjin to supervise collection of tribute grain and was granted preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: When sea transport was trial-tested, he was ordered to go to Tianjin to supervise collection of tribute grain and was granted preferential recognition.

sentences.zh: 七年，命在軍機大臣上學習行走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to study and serve under the Grand Council members.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered to study and serve under the Grand Council members.

sentences.zh: 逾年，張格爾就擒，加太子少保。

translations.literal: The following year, when Zhangge'er was captured, he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Zhangge'er was captured, he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 授軍機大臣，罷內務府大臣，直南書房。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Council member, relieved of duties as Household minister, and entered the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Council member, relieved of his duties as Household minister, and entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，歷兵部、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and successively served as minister of War and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and successively served as minister of War and of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十四年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he became associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 承修龍泉峪萬年吉地，工竣，晉太子太保，賜紫韁。

translations.literal: Supervising construction of the Longquan Valley imperial tomb, upon completion he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the purple reins.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising construction of the Longquan Valley imperial tomb, upon completion he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the purple reins.

sentences.zh: 十六年，充上書房總師傅，拜武英殿大學士，管理工部。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he became chief tutor of the Upper Study, was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence, and managed the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became chief tutor of the Upper Study, was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence, and managed the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十八年，晉文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 時禁煙議起，宣宗意銳甚，特命林則徐為欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦。

translations.literal: At that time debate over prohibiting opium arose; the Daoguang Emperor's resolve was sharp, and he specially commissioned Lin Zexu as imperial commissioner and sent him to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time debate over prohibiting opium arose; the Daoguang Emperor's resolve was sharp, and he specially commissioned Lin Zexu as imperial commissioner and sent him to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 英吉利領事義律初不聽約束，繼因停止貿易，始繳煙，盡焚之，責永不販運入境，強令具結，不從，兵釁遂開。

translations.literal: At first the English consul Charles Elliot would not submit to restrictions. Later, because trade was suspended, he began surrendering opium, which was all burned. He was required never again to smuggle opium into the country and was forced to give a written pledge; when he refused, hostilities broke out.
translations.idiomatic: At first the English consul Charles Elliot would not submit to restrictions. Later, because trade was suspended, he began surrendering opium, which was all burned. He was required never again to smuggle opium into the country and was forced to give a written pledge; when he refused, hostilities broke out.

sentences.zh: 則徐防禦嚴，不得逞於廣東，改犯閩、浙，沿海騷然。

translations.literal: Lin's defenses were strict, and they could not prevail in Guangdong, so they turned to attack Fujian and Zhejiang, and the coast was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's defenses were strict, and they could not prevail in Guangdong, so they turned to attack Fujian and Zhejiang, and the coast was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 英艦抵天津，投書總督琦善，言由則徐啟釁。

translations.literal: English warships reached Tianjin and delivered a letter to Governor Qishan, declaring that Lin had provoked the conflict.
translations.idiomatic: English warships reached Tianjin and delivered a letter to Governor Qishan, declaring that Lin had provoked the conflict.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿窺帝意移，乃贊和議，罷則徐，以琦善代之。

translations.literal: Mu Zhanga, seeing that the emperor's mind had shifted, then endorsed peace negotiations, removed Lin, and replaced him with Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zhanga, seeing that the emperor's mind had shifted, then endorsed peace negotiations, removed Lin, and replaced him with Qishan.

sentences.zh: 琦善一徇敵意，不設備，所要求者亦不盡得請，兵釁復起。

translations.literal: Qishan, yielding entirely to the enemy's wishes, made no preparations, and not all that was demanded was granted; hostilities broke out again.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan, yielding entirely to the enemy's wishes, made no preparations, and not all that was demanded was granted; hostilities broke out again.

sentences.zh: 先後命奕山、奕經督師，廣東、浙江皆挫敗​​。

translations.literal: Successively Yishan and Yijing were appointed to command the armies, but Guangdong and Zhejiang both suffered defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Successively Yishan and Yijing were appointed to command the armies, but Guangdong and Zhejiang both suffered defeats.

sentences.zh: 英兵且由海入江，林則徐及閩浙總督鄧廷楨、台灣總兵達洪阿、台灣道姚瑩以戰守為敵所忌，並被嚴譴，命伊里布、耆英、牛鑑議款。

translations.literal: English troops were moreover entering the Yangtze from the sea. Lin Zexu, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, Taiwan regional commander Da Hong'a, and Taiwan intendant Yao Ying—all disliked by the enemy for their defense of war—were all severely punished. Yilibu, Qiying, and Niu Jian were ordered to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: English troops were moreover entering the Yangtze from the sea. Lin Zexu, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, Taiwan regional commander Da Hong'a, and Taiwan intendant Yao Ying—all disliked by the enemy for their defense of war—were all severely punished. Yilibu, Qiying, and Niu Jian were ordered to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，和議成，償幣通商，各國相繼立約。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year peace was concluded: indemnities were paid and trade resumed, and various nations successively established treaties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year peace was concluded: indemnities were paid and trade resumed, and various nations successively established treaties.

sentences.zh: 國威既損，更喪國權，外患自此始。

translations.literal: National prestige was already diminished, and sovereign rights were further surrendered—foreign troubles began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige was already diminished, and sovereign rights were further surrendered—foreign troubles began from this point.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿當國，主和議，為海內所叢詬。

translations.literal: While Mu Zhanga held power, he advocated peace negotiations and was universally reviled throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: While Mu Zhanga held power, he advocated peace negotiations and was universally reviled throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 上既厭兵，從其策，終道光朝，恩眷不衰。

translations.literal: The emperor, already weary of war, followed his policy, and through the entire Daoguang reign his imperial favor never declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already weary of war, followed his policy, and through the entire Daoguang reign his imperial favor never declined.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶以來，典鄉試三，典會試五。

translations.literal: Since the Jiaqing reign he had thrice presided over provincial examinations and five times over metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing reign he had thrice presided over provincial examinations and five times over metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 凡覆試、殿試、朝考、教習庶吉士散館考差、大考翰詹，無歲不與衡文之役。

translations.literal: In every year he participated without fail in grading essays—re-examinations, palace examinations, palace audience examinations, Hanlin bachelors' graduation and assignment examinations, and grand examinations of the Hanlin and academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In every year he participated without fail in grading essays—re-examinations, palace examinations, palace audience examinations, Hanlin bachelors' graduation and assignment examinations, and grand examinations of the Hanlin and academicians.

sentences.zh: 國史、玉牒、實錄諸館，皆為總裁。

translations.literal: He served as chief compiler for the National History, Imperial Genealogy, Veritable Records, and other editorial offices.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief compiler for the National History, Imperial Genealogy, Veritable Records, and other editorial offices.

sentences.zh: 門生故吏遍於中外，知名之士多被援引，一時號曰「穆黨」。

translations.literal: His students and former subordinates spread throughout court and provinces; many renowned scholars were recommended by him; for a time they were called the "Mu faction."
translations.idiomatic: His protégés and old retainers filled posts at court and across the empire, and he placed many celebrated men in office—so that for a time they were known as the "Mu clique."

sentences.zh: 文宗自在潛邸深惡之，既即位十閱月，特詔數其罪曰：「穆彰阿身任大學士，受累朝知遇之恩，保位貪榮，妨賢病國。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor, already deeply loathing him while still heir apparent, ten months after ascending the throne issued a special edict enumerating his crimes, saying: "Mu Zhanga holds the post of grand secretary, received the grace of knowing favor from successive reigns, clings to his position and covets glory, obstructs the worthy and harms the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng Emperor had hated him bitterly even as crown prince. Ten months after his accession he issued a special edict listing Mu Zhanga's crimes: "Mu Zhanga serves as grand secretary. He enjoyed the trust and favor of several reigns, yet clung to office and pursued rank, blocking able men and injuring the state.

sentences.zh: 小忠小信，陰柔以售其奸；

translations.literal: Petty loyalty and petty trustworthiness, using softness and stealth to sell his treachery;
translations.idiomatic: He offered small favors and small courtesies, masking treachery behind a gentle, yielding manner;

sentences.zh: 偽學偽才，揣摩以逢主意。

translations.literal: Counterfeit learning and counterfeit talent, probing to match the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His learning and talent were a pretense; he studied the emperor's mind and shaped his words to please it.

sentences.zh: 從前夷務之興，傾排異己，深堪痛恨！

translations.literal: When foreign affairs arose in the past, he overturned and expelled those unlike himself—deeply to be hated!
translations.idiomatic: When foreign troubles first arose, he overturned the court and drove out all who differed from him—conduct deeply to be abhorred!

sentences.zh: 如達洪阿、姚瑩之盡忠盡力，有礙於己，必欲陷之；

translations.literal: Men like Da Hong'a and Yao Ying, who served with full loyalty and exertion—when they obstructed his interests, he invariably sought to entrap them;
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Da Hong'a and Yao Ying, who gave their utmost in loyal service, he sought to ruin whenever they stood in his way;

sentences.zh: 耆英之無恥喪良，同惡相濟，盡力全之。

translations.literal: Qiying's shamelessness and loss of integrity—sharing evil and aiding one another, he exerted all effort to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying, shameless and corrupt, he shielded to the utmost, the two of them aiding each other in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 固寵竊權，不可枚舉。

translations.literal: Clinging to favor and usurping power—the instances cannot be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: His hoarding of imperial favor and usurpation of authority are too many to count.

sentences.zh: 我皇考大公至正，惟以誠心待人，穆彰阿得肆行無忌。

translations.literal: My late father the emperor was supremely fair and upright, treating people only with sincere heart; Mu Zhanga was thus able to act without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: My late father, the Daoguang Emperor, was utterly fair and just and dealt with men in good faith—so Mu Zhanga was able to act without fear or limit.

sentences.zh: 若使聖明早燭其姦，必置重典，斷不姑容。

translations.literal: Had the sage sovereign early discerned his treachery, he would certainly have imposed severe punishment and never tolerated him.
translations.idiomatic: Had my father seen through his villainy in time, he would surely have punished him severely and never let him off.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿恃恩益縱，始終不悛。

translations.literal: Mu Zhanga, relying on favor, grew ever more unrestrained and to the end never repented.
translations.idiomatic: Banking on past favor, Mu Zhanga grew ever bolder and never changed his ways.

sentences.zh: 自朕親政之初，遇事模棱，緘口不言。

translations.literal: From the beginning of my personal rule, on encountering affairs he was equivocal and kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of my personal rule he was evasive on every issue and kept his mouth shut.

sentences.zh: 迨數月後，漸施其伎倆。

translations.literal: After several months, he gradually deployed his tricks.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a few months did he begin to work his schemes again.

sentences.zh: 英船至天津，猶欲引耆英為腹心以遂其謀，欲使天下群黎复遭荼毒。

translations.literal: When English ships reached Tianjin, he still wished to bring Qiying back as his trusted confidant to carry out his schemes, intending to make the common people of the realm again suffer torment.
translations.idiomatic: When British ships reached Tianjin, he still wanted to install Qiying as his right hand to carry out his designs—so that the people of the empire would once again suffer devastation.

sentences.zh: 其心陰險，實不可問！

translations.literal: His heart was dark and treacherous—truly beyond inquiry!
translations.idiomatic: His heart is so dark and treacherous that words fail!

sentences.zh: 潘世恩等保林則徐，屢言其'柔弱病軀，不堪錄用'；

translations.literal: Pan Shien and others protected Lin Zexu, repeatedly saying his 'frail, sick body cannot bear appointment';
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shien and his allies shielded Lin Zexu, repeatedly claiming that Lin's 'feeble, ailing frame made him unfit for office';

sentences.zh: 及命林則徐赴粵西剿匪，又言'未知能去否'。

translations.literal: When Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangxi to suppress bandits, they again said 'it is unknown whether he can go.'
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was ordered to Guangxi to suppress bandits, they again said, 'it remains to be seen whether he can even make the journey.'

sentences.zh: 偽言熒惑，使朕不知外事，罪實在此。

translations.literal: False words to delude and confuse, causing me not to know external affairs—the crime lies precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: With lying words they misled me and kept me in the dark about events beyond the capital—their guilt lies here above all.

sentences.zh: 若不立申國法，何以肅綱紀而正人心？

translations.literal: If the national laws are not promptly enforced, how can discipline be upheld and hearts set right?
translations.idiomatic: If I do not enforce the law at once, how can I restore order and set men's hearts straight?

sentences.zh: 又何以不負皇考付託之重？

translations.literal: And how can the weight of my late father's entrustment not be betrayed?
translations.idiomatic: And how can I honor the heavy trust my late father placed in me?

sentences.zh: 第念三朝舊臣，一旦置之重法，朕心實有不忍，從寬革職永不敘用。

translations.literal: Yet considering him an old minister across three reigns, to place him at once under severe law—my heart truly cannot bear it; leniently dismissed from office and never again considered for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is an old servant of three reigns, and to punish him with the full weight of the law at a stroke is more than I can bring myself to do. I therefore show leniency: he is dismissed from office and shall never again be considered for appointment.

sentences.zh: 其罔上行私，天下共見，朕不為已甚，姑不深問。

translations.literal: His deceiving the sovereign for private ends—all under heaven witnessed it; I will not go to extremes and for now will not press deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His deceit of the throne for private gain is plain to all the realm, but I will not press the matter to extremes and for now will not pursue it further.

sentences.zh: 朕熟思審處，計之久矣，不得已之苦衷，諸臣其共諒之！」

translations.literal: I have pondered and deliberated at length, planning for long; this is the bitter necessity—I ask all ministers to understand together!
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed this decision long and carefully. This painful compromise is unavoidable—I ask my ministers to understand!

sentences.zh: 詔下，天下稱快。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, all under heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, the whole empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，捐軍餉，予五品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, he contributed military funds and was given a fifth-rank official cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign he donated funds for the army and was granted a fifth-rank cap button in recognition.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子薩廉，光緒五年進士，由翰林官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Sa Lian, a jinshi in the fifth year of Guangxu, rose from the Hanlin Academy to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sa Lian, who earned his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Guangxu reign, rose through the Hanlin Academy to become vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 潘世恩，字芝軒，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Shien, style name Zhixuan, was a native of Wu County, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shien, whose style was Zhixuan, came from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, top jinshi of the first class, first place, appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign he took first place among the first-class jinshi graduates and was appointed reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，大考一等，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing, grand examination first class, promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiaqing reign he placed first class in the palace examination and was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 和珅以其青年上第有才望，欲招致之，世恩謝不與通。

translations.literal: Heshen, seeing that he had passed high at a young age and possessed talent and prestige, wished to recruit him; Shien declined and would not associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen, impressed that Shien had placed high on the examinations while still young and already showed talent and promise, tried to win him over; Shien politely refused and would have nothing to do with him.

sentences.zh: 以次當遷，和珅抑題本六閱月不上。

translations.literal: When by seniority he was due for promotion, Heshen suppressed his memorial of appointment for six months without submitting it.
translations.idiomatic: When his turn for promotion came due, Heshen held up the appointment memorial and kept it from the throne for six months.

sentences.zh: 仁宗親政，乃擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took personal rule, he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jiaqing Emperor took personal control of the government, Shien was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 一歲三遷至內閣學士，歷禮部、兵部、戶部、吏部侍郎，督雲南、浙江、江西學政。

translations.literal: In one year he was promoted three times to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, served successively as vice minister of Rites, War, Revenue, and Personnel, and supervised education in Yunnan, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he was promoted three times, reaching grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat. He served in turn as vice minister of the Ministries of Rites, War, Revenue, and Personnel, and supervised provincial examinations in Yunnan, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢工部尚書，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, promoted to minister of Works, transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Works and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服除，以父老乞養，會其子登鄉舉，具疏謝，坐未親詣京，降侍郎。

translations.literal: He returned home on his mother's death; when mourning ended, citing his father's old age he requested leave to care for him. His son simultaneously passed the provincial examination; he submitted a memorial of thanks but was demoted to vice minister for not having gone personally to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother, and when the mourning period ended he asked leave to care for his aged father. His son passed the provincial examination at the same time; Shien submitted a memorial of thanks but was demoted to vice minister because he had not gone to the capital in person.

sentences.zh: 帝鑑其孝思，仍允終養，居家十載。

translations.literal: The emperor, recognizing his filial devotion, still granted leave for final care; he lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing his filial intent, still granted him leave to care for his father at home, where he remained for ten years.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，父喪服闋，補吏部侍郎，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang, when mourning for his father ended, he was restored as vice minister of Personnel and transferred to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Daoguang reign, after his father's mourning period ended, he was restored as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and then transferred to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 再授工部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: Again appointed minister of Works, transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed minister of the Ministry of Works and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年，超拜體仁閣大學士，管理戶部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, exceptionally appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Hall, placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was elevated directly to grand secretary of the Tiren Hall and placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋命為軍機大臣，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward appointed Grand Councilor and concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Grand Council and concurrently made chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 晉東閣大學士，調管工部。

translations.literal: Advanced to grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, transferred to manage the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and transferred to oversee the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief tutor of the Upper Study and given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，晉武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, advanced to grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以八十壽晉太傅，賜紫韁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, on his eightieth birthday advanced to Grand Tutor, granted a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, on his eightieth birthday, he was promoted to Grand Tutor and granted the honor of a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 其明年，引疾，迭疏乞休，溫詔慰留，僅解機務。

translations.literal: The next year, citing illness, he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; a warm edict comforted and retained him, merely relieving him of Grand Council duties.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, pleading illness, he submitted memorial after memorial asking to retire. A gracious edict urged him to stay, but released him from Grand Council duties alone.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，復三疏，始得予告，食全俸，留其子京邸。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Wenzong Emperor ascended the throne, he again submitted three memorials and was at last granted leave to retire, receiving full salary; his son was kept at the capital residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, after the Xianfeng Emperor's accession, he submitted three more memorials and was finally granted retirement on full salary, with his son remaining at the family residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，鄉舉重逢，詔就近與順天鹿鳴宴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, on the second provincial success, he was ordered to attend the Lu ming banquet for Shuntian nearby.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, when he celebrated a second provincial success, he was invited by edict to attend the Lu ming banquet for Shuntian graduates at a nearby venue.

sentences.zh: 次年，復與恩榮宴。

translations.literal: The following year, he again attended the Enrong banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he attended the Enrong banquet as well.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，遣親王奠醊，入祀賢良祠，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died; a prince was dispatched to offer libation; he entered worship at the Hall of Worthies; posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died. A prince was sent to offer libations at his funeral. He was enshrined in the Hall of Worthies and given the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 世恩歷事四朝，迭掌文衡，備叨恩遇。

translations.literal: Shien served four reigns, repeatedly presided over literary examinations, and was abundantly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Shien served four emperors, presided over literary examinations again and again, and enjoyed imperial favor in full measure.

sentences.zh: 筦部務，安靜持大體。

translations.literal: Managing ministry affairs, he was quiet and upheld the broad principles.
translations.idiomatic: In managing ministry business he was steady and unobtrusive, keeping to the larger principles.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江將軍請增都爾特六屯，議地當游牧，開墾非計，不可許。

translations.literal: The Heilongjiang general requested adding six Dörbet colonies; deliberation held the land suitable for nomadic grazing and that opening cultivation was inadvisable—it could not be approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heilongjiang general proposed adding six Dörbet farming colonies, Shien argued that the land was meant for pastoral use and that opening it to cultivation was unwise—the request could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 言官奏山東鹽課請歸地丁，議山東場灶半毗連淮境，一歸地丁，聽民自運自銷，必為兩淮引課之累，不可行。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized that Shandong salt levies should revert to land-and-capitation tax; deliberation held that Shandong salt fields and furnaces were half contiguous with Huai territory—once reverted, allowing people to transport and sell on their own would inevitably burden Lianghuai salt certificate revenues; it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When censors proposed folding Shandong salt taxes into the land-and-capitation levy, he argued that Shandong's salt fields and furnaces bordered Huai salt territory; if the change allowed private transport and sale, Lianghuai's certificate revenues would suffer—and the plan could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 在樞廷凡十七年，益慎密，有所論列，終不告人。

translations.literal: In the Grand Council for seventeen years in all, he became ever more cautious and secretive; whatever he argued, he never told others in the end.
translations.idiomatic: During seventeen years on the Grand Council he grew ever more guarded; whatever positions he took in deliberation, he never disclosed them to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 海疆事起，林則徐所論奏，廷議多讚之；

translations.literal: When the coastal crisis arose, the memorials Lin Zexu submitted were mostly praised in court deliberations;
translations.idiomatic: When trouble erupted on the coast, court deliberations largely approved the memorials Lin Zexu submitted;

sentences.zh: 及穆彰阿主撫，世恩心以為非，不能顯與立異。

translations.literal: When Mu Zhanga advocated appeasement, Shien inwardly thought it wrong but could not openly stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Zhanga pushed for appeasement, Shien privately disagreed but could not openly break with him.

sentences.zh: 迨咸豐初詔舉人才，世恩已在告，疏言林則徐歷任封疆，有體有用，請徵召來京備用，並薦前任台灣道姚瑩，文宗韙之，於罪穆彰阿時猶舉其言。

translations.literal: When at the beginning of Xianfeng an edict called for recommending talent, Shien was already on leave; he memorialized that Lin Zexu, having served in frontier provinces, possessed both principle and practical ability, requesting he be summoned to the capital for appointment, and also recommended former Taiwan intendant Yao Ying. The Wenzong Emperor approved, and when condemning Mu Zhanga still cited his words.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict at the start of the Xianfeng reign called for recommending talent, Shien was already retired. He memorialized that Lin Zexu, with long service in frontier provinces, combined sound judgment with practical ability, and asked that Lin be summoned to the capital for appointment; he also recommended the former Taiwan intendant Yao Ying. The Xianfeng Emperor approved, and when condemning Mu Zhanga he still quoted Shien's words.

sentences.zh: 次子曾瑩，道光二十一年進士，由編修官至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His second son Zengying, jinshi in the twenty-first year of Daoguang, rose from compiler to vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zengying, a jinshi graduate of the twenty-first year of the Daoguang reign, rose from compiler to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 孫祖廕，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Zuyin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zuyin is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：守成之世，治尚綜覈，而振敝舉衰，非拘守繩墨者所克任也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In eras of preserving the inheritance, governance favors comprehensive examination, yet to revive what is worn and lift what is declining is not a task those bound by rules can fulfill.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In ages devoted to preserving what has been achieved, government prizes thorough, comprehensive administration—but to revive what is worn out and lift what is failing is work that men chained to precedent cannot perform.

sentences.zh: 況運會平陂相乘，非常之變，往往當承平既久，萌蘗蠢兆於其間，馭之無術，措置張皇，而庸佞之輩，轉以彌縫迎合售其欺，其召亂可倖免哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, when cycles of ease and decline multiply, extraordinary upheavals often arise just when long peace has endured—sprouts of disorder stir in its midst. Governing without method, acting in panic, while mediocre flatterers instead use patching and compliance to sell their deceit—could turmoil thereby be luckily avoided?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, fortune turns between calm and decline in succession, and extraordinary crises often appear just when long peace has bred complacency—trouble sprouts in the cracks. When rulers lack the skill to master events and govern in panic, mediocre flatterers patch over problems and curry favor to sell their deceptions—is it any wonder that disorder follows?

sentences.zh: 宣宗初政，一倚曹振鏞，兢兢文法；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuanzong reign, relying solely on Cao Zhenyong, scrupulously observing literary formalities;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daoguang reign the emperor relied wholly on Cao Zhenyong and governed with scrupulous attention to formal precedent;

sentences.zh: 及穆彰阿柄用，和戰游移，遂成外患。

translations.literal: When Mu Zhanga wielded power, vacillating between peace and war, external troubles thus took shape.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Zhanga came to power and wavered between war and peace, foreign calamity took root.

sentences.zh: 一代安危，斯其關鍵已。

translations.literal: The safety or peril of an age—here lay the pivotal hinge.
translations.idiomatic: The rise or fall of an era turned on this hinge.

sentences.zh: 英和才不竟用，王鼎忠貞致身，文孚、潘世恩皆恪恭保位者耳。

translations.literal: Ying He's talent was never fully employed; Wang Ding gave his life in loyal devotion; Wen Fu and Pan Shien were merely those who dutifully preserved their positions.
translations.idiomatic: Ying He's talent was never fully used; Wang Ding gave his life in loyal remonstrance; Wen Fu and Pan Shien were men who kept their posts through dutiful compliance—and nothing more.
